clue.text: Lives quietly at first and sits in chair?

indicators.note: says the quiet letter goes at the front of the word for lives

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for playing quietly
to reside somewhere is to live there

explanation.surface: Someone living a quiet life who spends the day sitting in an armchair.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'sits in chair' means taking the chair of a meeting, not lounging.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who takes the chair at a meeting is in charge of proceedings, which is the verb's meaning.

clue.text: Fear of pagan deity in charge

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and the wild

explanation.surface: Dread of a heathen god who runs things.
explanation.walkthrough: Fittingly, the word for sudden terror comes from Pan, said to cause it in lonely places.
explanation.definitionFit: Sudden overwhelming dread is a synonym of fear, often spreading through a crowd.

clue.text: Gentleman rated highly said to be astonished

indicators.note: tells us the words for gentleman and rated highly are heard rather than written

parts.note: a gentleman is addressed as SIR, and rated highly is PRIZED; spoken together they make the answer

explanation.surface: A well-regarded gentleman is reported to be amazed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said to be' marks two homophones: SIR for the knight and PRIZED for rated highly; run together, they sound like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken aback by something unexpected is a synonym of being astonished.

clue.text: 24-hour protection needed? This help isn't available overnight

parts.note: a day is a period of twenty-four hours
care is looking after and protecting someone

explanation.surface: Round-the-clock protection is needed, but this service shuts at night.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pits '24-hour' against 'overnight': the day is a full 24 hours, but the service runs only in daytime.
explanation.definitionFit: Nurseries and centres that look after children or the elderly in working hours send everyone home at night.

clue.text: Act as a proud bird might and find new things to do

definitions.text: Act as a proud bird might
definitions.meaning: a bird showing off, like a peacock, opens out its feathers fully
the idiom for trying new experiences and becoming independent

explanation.definitionFit: A bird literally stretches out its feathers; figuratively the phrase means venturing into new activities.

clue.text: Show respect for nineteenth eleven, as you might say?

indicators.note: signals that the letter name and the team are spoken aloud to give the answer

parts.note: S is the nineteenth letter of the alphabet, and an eleven is a sports TEAM; spoken, the letter and the team run together

explanation.surface: Honouring a nineteenth cricket or football side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nineteenth' is the letter S, pronounced 'ess'; 'eleven' is a team. Said together, 'ess team' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To hold someone in high regard is to respect and admire them.

clue.text: No longer obvious what one must do to make things clear

parts.note: EX is the prefix for former, something no longer so
plain means clear or obvious

explanation.surface: Something no longer evident needs spelling out so it can be understood.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something clear is to account for it or make it understandable, the verb's meaning.

clue.text: Title is special — does one ignore ordinary folk?

definitions.note: the definition asks for a noun: a person who looks down on ordinary people

indicators.note: made special or reworked, so the letters of title is are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grand title is something special: does its holder snub the common people?
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who believes in rule by a select few tends to disdain the masses.

clue.text: Beasts in a good lake descended on by soldiers

indicators.note: in a down clue the soldiers come down on top, so their word sits first

parts.note: MEN is a common crossword word for soldiers, the ranks
Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: Animals by a lake are attacked by an army.
explanation.definitionFit: A collection of wild animals kept for show is a group of beasts.

clue.text: Lord settled in US city? Not quite

indicators.note: the peer moves into the city, so his title goes inside it

parts.note: NY is New York
an earl is a lord, a peer of the realm

explanation.surface: A British aristocrat has made his home in New York, though not entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: Almost but not fully is the meaning of the adverb, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Pair wandering around Iran having accident by river

indicators.note: the letters of pair wander around into a new order
Iran suffers a mishap and its letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A couple roaming Iran meet with a mishap near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by river' is the whole definition: the answer is an adjective for riverbanks, not a word for a river.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes things on or beside a riverbank, such as plants or land rights.

clue.text: Endless work to get information on certain animals

indicators.note: the word for work loses its final letter

parts.note: a chore is a piece of routine work
data is information

explanation.surface: Never-ending research to gather facts about particular creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts the last letter from CHORE, leaving CHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The phylum is the zoological group of animals with a notochord, including all vertebrates.

clue.text: Welshman heading off with group for broadcast

indicators.note: the name loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: Dai is a typical Welsh man's name in crosswords
a ring is a group, as of conspirators

explanation.surface: A Welshman leaves with his band to go on the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the first letter of DAI, leaving AI.
explanation.definitionFit: A transmission on radio or television is a broadcast, the noun's sense here.

clue.text: Successful in life? Not American fellow stranded on island

indicators.note: says the American letters are left out of the word for successful

parts.note: prosperous means thriving and successful

explanation.surface: A man marooned on an island wonders whether he has done well in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' drops US from PROSPEROUS. The definition points to Shakespeare's The Tempest, whose magician lives exiled on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: The deposed Duke of Milan in The Tempest is cast away on an island with his daughter.

clue.text: Bird erring badly when diving into water

indicators.note: the jumbled letters plunge into the word for water

parts.note: pee is a slang word for urine, a crossword staple for water

indicators.note: the letters of erring are put together badly, in a new order

explanation.surface: A bird of prey makes a mistake as it dives into a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'water' is the crossword's cheeky slang for urine, not a lake or sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The falcon is a fast bird of prey, famous for its stooping dive.

clue.text: Rabbit found in train at terminus

definitions.note: as a verb, rabbit is British slang for chatter on

indicators.note: the answer is found inside the run of letters of train at terminus

explanation.surface: A rabbit discovered on a train when it reaches the end of the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' looks like the animal, but in British slang (from 'rabbit and pork', rhyming with talk) it means to talk on and on.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words are British slang verbs for chatting idly at length.

clue.text: Quality of slow service with sailor needing to eat on ship

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
to dine is to eat a meal
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Slow restaurant service on a liner where a sailor wants a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateness or slowness is the quality of service that keeps diners waiting.

clue.text: Pole that is restricting a traveller

indicators.note: the pole and the abbreviation close round the a, holding it in

parts.note: a rod is a pole
IE is id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A Pole holding a traveller back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' tempts as a nationality, but it is a rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a band's touring crew travels from venue to venue setting up the equipment.

clue.text: By no means resembling a rounded character

definitions.text: By no means resembling a rounded character

parts.words: By no means resembling a rounded character
parts.note: something far from rounded has sharp corners and straight lines; for a person, it suggests a bony, lean figure

explanation.definitionFit: Having sharp corners and straight edges is the opposite of being curved or rounded.

clue.text: Recluse has some productive time reflecting when standing on head

indicators.note: in a down entry the hidden run is turned upside down, read from bottom to top
only some of the letters of productive time reflecting are used

explanation.surface: A hermit spends time in quiet reflection, even doing headstands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' hides ETIMERE in 'productivE TIME REflecting'; 'when standing on head' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit, especially a religious one living alone, is a recluse.

clue.text: Stop with gold and meet authorised receiver

parts.note: an end is a stop
OR is gold in heraldry
to see someone is to meet them

explanation.surface: Halt with the gold and meet the official recipient.
explanation.definitionFit: The person to whom a cheque or bill is signed over is entitled to receive payment.

clue.text: Unlimited desire to enter fellow's place of confinement

indicators.note: the trimmed desire goes into the fellow

parts.note: a don is a fellow of a university college

indicators.note: the word for desire loses its outer letters

parts.note: hunger is a strong desire

explanation.surface: A man's boundless lust leads him to a prison.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a fellow, a senior teacher at an Oxford or Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: A dark underground cell for holding prisoners is a place of confinement.

clue.text: Geese in high wind to keep going in extremis

indicators.note: the wind holds those letters inside it

parts.note: a gale is a strong wind

indicators.note: only the extreme letters, first and last, of going are taken

explanation.surface: Geese battling a gale to keep flying at the last gasp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in extremis' is Latin for at the point of death, here read literally as 'at the extremes' of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A flock of geese on the ground is known by this collective noun.

clue.text: Capital city in Caribbean containing pub with little spirit

indicators.note: the Caribbean letters hold the pub

parts.note: WI is the West Indies
an inn is a pub
a peg is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A capital city on a Caribbean island with a bar serving a tot of rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caribbean' tempts toward an island capital, but the city is in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the capital of the Canadian province of Manitoba.

clue.text: Toothy beast jumping at oranges — only some taken

indicators.note: just part of the letters of jumping at oranges are used

explanation.surface: A large-jawed animal leaps at oranges, eating only a few.
explanation.definitionFit: The short informal name for an alligator, a reptile with many large teeth.

clue.text: Trick that's bad played on us — I'll get caught

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill will

indicators.note: the I is caught inside the reworked letters
on us is played with, its letters reworked

parts.note: read as I will: the letter I

explanation.surface: A dirty trick has been played on us, and I'm going to be found out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll get caught' reads as 'I will get caught': the letter I is held inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror's trick deceives the eye, creating a false impression.

clue.text: They go out in pursuit when leader's gone missing by river

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: the word for pursuit loses its first letter

parts.note: a hunt is a pursuit

explanation.surface: People chasing someone leave when their leader disappears near a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the Latin stage direction meaning that actors leave the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: In play scripts this Latin direction tells several characters to leave the stage.

clue.text: Anger? It's that bad before peace finally comes

indicators.note: the word just given is in a bad way, its letters jumbled
only the closing letter of peace is used

explanation.surface: Is it anger? It's that bad until peace finally arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anger' does double duty, as definition and as the fodder that 'It's that bad' scrambles into ENRAG.
explanation.definitionFit: To anger someone is to make them furious, a verb sense.

clue.text: Boy gets confused — last requirement for actor or performer

parts.note: a son is a boy

indicators.note: the letters of gets are confused into a new order
only the final letter of actor is wanted

explanation.surface: A lad is muddled about the final thing an actor or performer needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges GETS into GSTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A singer is a performer of songs.
